Sodium lauryl sulfate, in turn, targets Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3. This chain of interactions implies that Aminophenazone may influence the activity of Potassium voltage-gated channels through its effect on the potassium-transporting ATPase subunit beta, which could modulate the function of these channels. The indirect pathway suggests that Aminophenazone may act as a modulator of potassium channel activity, potentially affecting cellular signaling and ion transport. The strength of the evidence is moderate, as the relationships are inferred through target-based associations, and further experimental validation would be necessary to confirm the direct interaction between Aminophenazone and Potassium voltage-gated channel subfamily D member 3.
